Users should still replace placeholders carefully and manage Azure credentials outside source control.

content.value_statement: Azure authentication choices can be confusing across local development, CI, and hosted workloads. This skill guides Java developers through Azure Identity credential patterns and safer configuration.
actual_capabilities: Explains DefaultAzureCredential order and common builder options.
Shows Java authentication examples for managed identity and service principals.
Lists Azure Identity environment variables and certificate settings.
Compares credential choices for local, Azure-hosted, CI, and desktop applications.
Covers workload identity, token caching, sovereign clouds, logging, and error handling.
limitations: Does not validate live Azure tenants, app registrations, or role assignments.
Does not execute Java, Maven, Azure CLI, or PowerShell commands.
Uses the SDK version shown in the skill file, which may need updating.
Does not manage secrets, certificates, tokens, or access policies.

use_cases.title: Add Azure SDK Authentication
use_cases.description: Use the skill to choose and configure a credential for a Java service using Azure clients.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Identity
use_cases.description: Use the managed identity guidance to avoid long-lived secrets in Azure-hosted Java applications.

use_cases.title: Configure CI Authentication
use_cases.description: Use the environment credential notes to prepare service principal authentication for pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Default Credentials
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use DefaultAzureCredential in a Java application that connects to Azure Storage.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Credential Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the right pattern for a deployment environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare managed identity, environment credential, and service principal authentication for this Java deployment: [describe environment].

prompt_templates.title: Review Secret Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Java Azure authentication approach and identify where managed identity or workload identity would reduce secret exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Credential Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture across development, CI, and production.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Azure Identity strategy for a Java service that runs locally, in CI, and on AKS with workload identity.

output_examples.input: Which credential should I use for a Java app on Azure App Service?
output_examples.output: A concise recommendation to use managed identity through DefaultAzureCredential, with notes on client IDs and required Azure roles.

output_examples.input: How should my pipeline authenticate to Azure from Java tests?
output_examples.output: A checklist of service principal environment variables, secret storage cautions, and when to prefer federated identity.

output_examples.input: Why does my local DefaultAzureCredential fail?
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path covering tenant selection, Azure CLI login state, excluded credentials, and authentication logging.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential during development and managed identity in production.
Grant only the Azure roles required by the Java application.
Store secrets and certificates in managed secret stores, not source files.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding client secrets, tenant IDs, or certificate passwords in Java source.
Using service principal secrets for Azure-hosted applications that support managed identity.
Enabling verbose authentication logs in production without reviewing sensitive output.

faq.question: What Java package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers com.azure:azure-identity, the Azure Identity library for Java applications.

faq.question: Does it run Azure CLI commands?
faq.answer: No. It documents Azure CLI credential behavior but does not execute commands.

faq.question: Can it replace Azure documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as implementation guidance and verify current SDK details with official Azure documentation.

faq.question: Does it include real credentials?
faq.answer: No. The file uses placeholders for tenant IDs, client IDs, secrets, and certificate paths.

faq.question: When should I use managed identity?
faq.answer: Use managed identity for Azure-hosted workloads when the service supports it and role assignments are available.

faq.question: Is workload identity covered?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes AKS workload identity guidance and the related Azure Identity settings.
